source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 22. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: The boy who cried “Tiger!” — and why a lie is always a lie

learn.en: A boy guarding sheep shouted “Help! A tiger!” The villagers ran out with sticks — but there was no tiger, and he laughed at them.
learn.title: The boy who cried “Tiger!”

learn.en: He did it again. Then a real tiger came. “Help!” he shouted — but nobody came. He had lied so often that no one believed him.
learn.title: Nobody believes a liar

learn.en: A lie is a word, sign or action that shows the opposite of the truth, usually to trick others. A liar soon finds he has no true friends.
learn.title: What is a lie?

learn.en: A mother called her son: “Come, I'll give you something.” The Prophet ﷺ asked what. “Some dates.” He said: if you give him nothing, it is written as a lie.
learn.title: Even small lies

learn.en: A lie is a lie, however small — even to make people laugh or to escape trouble. Allah dislikes lying.
learn.title: A lie is a lie

learn.en: “They only invent falsehood who do not believe in the verses of Allah.” (Qur'an 16:105)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

quiz.en: Why did the villagers not come the last time?
opts: He had lied so often that nobody believed him

quiz.en: True or false? I may lie to make people laugh.
True or false? It is OK to lie to keep myself out of trouble.
True or false? Allah dislikes telling lies.
True or false? We must give up lying and always tell the truth.

think.q: Why do you think it is so important that people can believe what you say?
think.a: So they trust you and come when you really need help — like the boy who needed help with the real tiger.

parents.summary: The boy who cried “Tiger!”: liars lose trust. A lie is a lie, even a small or “funny” one — Allah dislikes lying.
parents.tip: Retell the tiger story together and ask him what the boy should have done.
